description: Routing corpus for the unified skill-lifecycle tool (author/edit/optimize + score/critique/eval). Rebuilt 2026-05-31 for the v3.0.0 meta-skill fold: triggers cover both authoring and evaluation; adversarials route to the specialized authors and adjacent skills that remain separate.
trigger_phrases: complete review of this skill using skills-studio
thorough review of {skill} using skills-studio
full review of this skill
promote this skill to stable
is this skill ready to promote?
comprehensive evaluation of this skill
run the full review on {skill}
create a skill for [domain]
build a new skill that does Y
help me write a SKILL.md for a code-review assistant
turn this workflow into a reusable skill
edit this skill — it's routing wrong
improve / optimize this skill's description for triggering accuracy
create skill.json and a routing corpus for my new skill
score this skill against best practices
rubric audit / best-practices scorecard for this skill
run the 9-critic panel on this skill
run a Boris review on this skill
what would Elon delete from this skill?
adversarial eval of this skill / Simon Willison security review
which dimensions fail for this skill?
measure this skill's performance with test cases and variance
benchmark this skill across prompts
adversarial_phrases: build a comprehensive domain-expert skill like ref-dashboard
make a knowledge-base reference skill for [domain] with research waves
build a peer-reviewed academic theory skill
write a PRD for this feature
audit my repo for stale docs
design a new MCP server for our API
design the orchestration loop for this goal
notes: Adversarials route to siblings that stay separate: comprehensive domain-expert / knowledge-base skills → meta-expert-author; peer-reviewed theory skills → meta-theory-author; PRDs → plan-prd; repo doc audits → ops-repo; MCP design → core-mcp-best-practices; agent-loop orchestration → core-agent-loops. skills-studio owns the general skill lifecycle — authoring, scoring, critiquing, and measuring skills themselves.
